name: Sicilian: Alapin
description: Your White answer to the Sicilian: 2.c3 prepares d4 and sidesteps the big Open Sicilian theory.

lines.name: 2…Nc6

notes.2: c3 prepares d4, so White can take back on d4 with a pawn and keep a big centre.
notes.4: d4: White gets the big centre the Alapin aims for.
notes.10: Nf3 develops with the queen on d5 exposed in the centre.

10.Nc3: …Qxd4 grabs the pawn; Nf3 first keeps d4 protected.

lines.summary: Against 2…Nc6, take the centre with d4 and cxd4; after …d5, take and develop Nf3.

lines.name: 2…Nc6: 6…Bg4

notes.2: c3 prepares d4, so White can take back on d4 with a pawn and keep a big centre.
notes.4: d4: White gets the big centre the Alapin aims for.
notes.10: Nf3 develops with the queen on d5 exposed in the centre.
notes.12: Nc3 develops with tempo on the black queen.
notes.14: gxf3 takes back; after the queen trade on d4, the c3 knight jumps to b5.
notes.18: Nb5 attacks the d4 knight and threatens Nc7+.

10.Nc3: …Qxd4 grabs the pawn; Nf3 first keeps d4 protected.

18.Bd3: …Nxf3+! grabs a pawn with check; Nb5 first keeps Black busy.

lines.summary: Against the pin, develop Nc3 with tempo on the queen; after the trades, Nb5 hits c7 and d4.

lines.name: 6…Bg4 7…Qd8

notes.2: c3 prepares d4, so White can take back on d4 with a pawn and keep a big centre.

notes.12: Nc3 develops with tempo on the black queen.
notes.14: d5! kicks the c6 knight, and Black's pieces get tangled: Qa4+ and Bb5+ are coming.

10.Nc3: …Qxd4 grabs the pawn; Nf3 first keeps d4 protected.

lines.summary: When the queen retreats, d5! kicks the knight and the checks on a4 and b5 win material.

lines.name: 4…e6

notes.4: d4: White gets the big centre the Alapin aims for.
notes.10: e5 gains space: a French-style structure with an extra tempo for White.

lines.name: 2…d5

notes.2: c3 prepares d4, so White can take back on d4 with a pawn and keep a big centre.
notes.6: d4: the queen on d5 can't take back on c3 because of the c-pawn.
notes.10: Be2 breaks the pin on the f3 knight in advance.
notes.12: O-O: White's king is safe; the centre is White's.

lines.summary: Against 2…d5, take on d5, push d4, then Nf3, Be2 and castle.

notes.10: Be2 develops quietly; O-O and c4 or Be3 come next.

lines.summary: If Black skips the pin, develop with Be2 and castle; White keeps a nice centre.
